title: How can we refine the number system we made earlier?
description: A system of one mark for every object is refined by giving new symbols to groups and to groups of groups, the way the Roman symbols are landmark numbers. The video tests the new system on thirty seven objects and checks that the numeral is shorter and still right. Any sensible refinement is welcome.
teaching_notes: One idea: add landmark numbers to a system that has one mark for each object. A symbol for a group and a symbol for a group of groups shorten every numeral. Watch for students who add symbols but forget to say what each one is worth.

source: Figure it Out (early number systems, question 4)
video_script.why: The child uses the idea of landmark numbers from the solved example to make an earlier tally system shorter.
video_script.substitution: Give a new symbol to a group, then to a group of groups, and write a number by taking the biggest landmark first.

maths_rules: the earlier system has one mark for every object, so 37 objects need 37 marks
a circle stands for a group of 5 marks
a square stands for a group of 5 circles, which is 25 marks
37 = 25 + 5 + 5 + 1 + 1, written as 1 square, 2 circles and 2 marks, 5 symbols in all
check: 25 + 10 + 2 = 37 and 5 symbols are fewer than 37 marks
